ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a certain grain depot uses an electric conveyor to transport sack packages onto a grain stack. Now a sack package is placed on the inclined conveyor belt and moves upward at a uniform speed together with the conveyor belt. During this, a fault suddenly occurs, and the conveyor belt decelerates until it stops. If, during the above uniform-speed and deceleration processes, the sack package and the conveyor belt always remain relatively stationary, which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When moving at a uniform speed, the friction force on the sack package must be upward along the conveyor belt

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a certain grain depot uses an electric conveyor to transport sack packages onto a grain stack. Now a sack package is placed on the inclined conveyor belt and moves upward at a uniform speed together with the conveyor belt. If the sack package and the conveyor belt always remain relatively stationary, then when moving at a uniform speed, in what direction along the conveyor belt is the friction force on the sack package?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When moving at a uniform speed, the friction force on the sack package must be upward along the conveyor belt
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, one can see an inclined electric conveyor belt extending obliquely upward from a lower place to above the grain stack, and the sack package is placed on the inclined belt surface; the conveyor belt is used to transport the sack package upward. Then reason: The question stem states that the sack package moves upward at a uniform speed together with the conveyor belt, and always remains relatively stationary. Analyzing the sack package along the direction of the conveyor belt, gravity has a component along the inclined plane downward along the conveyor belt; uniform motion means that the resultant force on the sack package along the inclined-plane direction is zero. If there were no friction force, the sack package would have a tendency to slide downward relative to the conveyor belt, so the static friction force must be upward along the conveyor belt, to balance the downward component of gravity along the inclined plane.
